blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Self-evolving language models train on tasks they generate, so every round must decide which updated model the next round inherits. Current loops such as R-Zero, Agent0, and Skill Self-Play make this decision through the task, admitting tasks that look learnable and inheriting every resulting update. We identify a selection-to-update gap in these loops, where a task that looks learnable need not produce a useful update. Most updates on verified tasks fail to make correct answers more likely, yet these loops inherit them all. HeirCommit freezes the updated model and uses fresh evaluation questions to decide whether to inherit it or retain the current model. EvoHeir separates parameter inheritance from experience inheritance, using current and archived experience to repair failures and preserve successes before final confirmation. Our analysis characterizes selection-induced optimism and decomposes regret into selection, absorption, and confirmation errors. HeirCommit cuts the harmful share of accepted updates by 68-83% relative to random inheritance at the same acceptance rate. Across four backbones, EvoHeir achieves the best mathematics and general-reasoning averages, raising the math average by 5.3% relative to the strongest baseline, Agent0. The framework lets useful experience persist even when the model that produced it is not inherited.
blocks.zh: 自我演变的语言模型列车在他们产生的任务上,所以每一回合都必须决定下一轮继承哪个更新的模型. 当前循环如R-Zero,Agent0和Skill Self-Play通过任务来做出这个决定,承认看起来可以学习的任务,并继承了每个由此产生的更新. 我们发现在这些循环中存在一个选择更新的空白,一个看起来可以学习的任务不需要产生有用的更新. 关于已核实任务的多数更新未能使正确的答案更可能,然而这些循环继承了它们的全部. HeirCommitt冻结了更新的模型,并使用新的评价问题来决定是继承还是保留目前的模型. EvoHeir将参数继承与经验继承区分开来,使用当前和存档的经验来修复失败,并在最终确认之前保存成功. 我们的分析定性为选择引起的乐观,并将遗憾分解为选择、吸收和确认错误。 与随机继承相比,Heir承诺将接受更新的有害份额减少68-83%,接受率相同. Our contributions are: 1. We identify the selection-to-update gap and
prove that pre-update behavior alone cannot identify an update’s
value.
Reusing screening evidence to accept a branch pays a union bound over branches,
which fresh confirmation removes. 2. We introduce HeirCommit , a source-independent rule that commits a
frozen successor only when it beats the current model on fresh probes. On the
native updates of R-Zero, Agent0, and Skill-SP, it turns negative pool gain
positive on two of the three hosts. 3. We develop EvoHeir , which decides separately which parameters the
next learner inherits and which experience it absorbs. Across four backbones it
raises the base model’s math average by 7.9–30.1%, the most of
any compared method. 4. We show that experience outlives the model that produced it .

average, and experience from rounds whose model was rejected adds 0.66 pp
beyond committed-round history.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
We identify the selection-to-update gap: admitting a
task that looks learnable does not ensure a useful update, and
60 of 96 updates on verified tasks show
no gain. HeirCommit inherits a successor only when it beats the current model on
fresh probes and cuts the harmful share of commits by 68–83% on
three self-evolution hosts. EvoHeir separates the parameters a round inherits
from the experience it keeps and raises the math average by up to
7.0% over Agent0, the strongest baseline. Self-evolving systems
should judge the updates they produce, not only the tasks they choose, and keep
experience beyond the models that produced it.

blocks.en:
Recovery eligibility uses training-role records, response completion, answer
verification, and reference provenance, and excludes known contradictory
problems, wrong labels, and erroneous references. Screening and confirmation
are numerical decisions on fresh responses: the runs contain no
natural-language judge prompt and no model-generated accept or reject
decision. External benchmarks use their frozen standard instructions, and
their prompts, responses, and results never enter training, memory, screening,
or confirmation.
